grammarOverview.summary: In present affirmative equative sentences ("X is Y"), no verb "to be" is required. The particle "бол" or "нь" or direct juxtaposing is used.
keyPoints: Subject + Object / Predicate Noun (e.g. Би оюутан = I am a student)
Subject + бол + Predicate Noun (emphasis / topic: Энэ бол ном = This is a book)
Subject + нь + Predicate Noun (declarative focus: Тэр нь эмч = He is a doctor)

grammarOverview.summary: Expresses possession, origin, or association ("of / 's"). Formed with -ын/-ийн/-ний/-ны depending on terminal phonemes.
keyPoints: Consonant stems (masculine): + ын (e.g. адуу -> адууны, ном -> номын)
Consonant stems (feminine): + ийн (e.g. гэр -> гэрийн, эгч -> эгчийн)
Stems ending in long vowels or diphthongs: + н / -ны / -ний
Stems ending in short vowels: usually drop final short vowel + ын/ийн

grammarOverview.summary: Indicates the indirect object ("to"), static location ("in, at, on"), or time of occurrence ("at, on, in").
keyPoints: Words ending in vowels, semi-vowels, or resonant consonants (м, н, л, б, в): + д (e.g. сургуульд, гэрт)
Words ending in voiceless obstruents (г, р, с, д, т, ц, ч, х): + т (e.g. гэрт, хотод)

rules.title: Dative-Locative Case (Өгөх оршихын тийн ялгал: -д, -т)
rules.summary: Indicates the indirect object ("to"), static location ("in, at, on"), or time of occurrence ("at, on, in").
rules.explanation: Indicates the indirect object ("to"), static location ("in, at, on"), or time of occurrence ("at, on, in").

examples.english: I live in Ulaanbaatar.
Gave a book to younger sibling.
Let's meet at five o'clock.

exceptions: Using accusative instead of dative-locative for static location (*Би хотыг байна is incorrect; use Би хотод байна).
Misapplying -д after -р (*гэрд is wrong; correct is гэрт).

grammarOverview.summary: Marks the definite direct object of a transitive verb. Indefinite direct objects may appear in the unmarked (zero) form.
keyPoints: Vowel ending: + г (e.g. аав -> аавыг, ээж -> ээжийг, нохой -> нохойг)
Consonant ending (masculine): + ыг (e.g. ном -> номыг, мал -> малыг)
Consonant ending (feminine): + ийг (e.g. сүү -> сүүг, цэцэг -> цэцгийг)

rules.title: Accusative Case (Заахын тийн ялгал: -ыг, -ийг, -г)
rules.summary: Marks the definite direct object of a transitive verb. Indefinite direct objects may appear in the unmarked (zero) form.
rules.explanation: Marks the definite direct object of a transitive verb. Indefinite direct objects may appear in the unmarked (zero) form.

examples.english: I read this specific book.
Called one's mother.
Will you drink water? (indefinite - zero case)

exceptions: Adding accusative to indefinite general objects (*Би алим идмээр байна vs Би энэ алимыг идмээр байна).
Vowel harmony violations (*гэрыг is wrong, correct is гэрийг).

grammarOverview.summary: Signifies point of departure ("from"), origin, material, cause, or the standard in comparative constructions ("than").
keyPoints: Masculine unrounded: + аас (e.g. ааваас, сургуулиас)
Feminine unrounded: + ээс (e.g. гэрээс, ээжээс)
Masculine rounded (о): + оос (e.g. хотоос, олноос)
Feminine rounded (ө): + өөс (e.g. өдрөөс, өвөөс)

rules.title: Ablative Case (Гарахын тийн ялгал: -аас, -ээс, -оос, -өөс)
rules.summary: Signifies point of departure ("from"), origin, material, cause, or the standard in comparative constructions ("than").
rules.explanation: Signifies point of departure ("from"), origin, material, cause, or the standard in comparative constructions ("than").

examples.english: I came from the countryside.
An apple fell from the tree.
This book is more interesting than that book.

exceptions: Ignoring labial harmony: writing *хотоос as *хотаас.
Confusing comparative standard case: Mongolian uses Ablative for "than" (e.g. Ааваас өндөр = taller than father).

Verb stem ending in voiceless consonant (с, х, ц, ч, т): + ч байна (e.g. бичиж байна, сууж байна, нисч байна)

rules.explanation: Replaces 3rd person and 1st/2nd person possessives when the possessor is the subject of the same clause ("one's own").

examples.english: I am going towards my own home.
He helped his own younger sibling.
The herder went to his own livestock.

exceptions: Using 3rd person genitive түүний when referring to the subject's own possession (*Тэр түүний номыг уншив instead of номоо).
Violating vowel harmony across four variants (-аа, -ээ, -оо, -өө).

grammarOverview.summary: Specifies movement towards a general direction or target destination ("towards, in the direction of").
keyPoints: Words not ending in -р: + руу (masculine), + рүү (feminine)
Words ending in -р: + луу (masculine), + лүү (feminine) to prevent double "r" clash (e.g. гэр -> гэр лүү)

rules.title: Directional Case (Чиглэхийн тийн ялгал: -руу, -рүү / -луу, -лүү)
rules.summary: Specifies movement towards a general direction or target destination ("towards, in the direction of").
rules.explanation: Specifies movement towards a general direction or target destination ("towards, in the direction of").

examples.english: I will go towards the city.
We returned towards our home.
Walked up the mountain, towards the river.

exceptions: Writing *гэр рүү instead of dissimilated гэр лүү.
Confusing with Dative-Locative -д/-т which denotes arriving AT the point, whereas -руу emphasizes motion TOWARDS.

keyPoints: Verb Stem + -сан (masculine non-labial: явсан, харсан)
Verb Stem + -сэн (feminine non-labial: ирсэн, үзсэн)
Verb Stem + -сон (masculine labial: орсон, бодсон)
Verb Stem + -сөн (feminine labial: өгсөн, төрсөн)

rules.title: Past Tense Participle (-сан, -сэн, -сон, -сөн)
rules.summary: Expresses completed action in the past, or acts as a past attributive participle ("having done"). 4-way harmony.
rules.explanation: Expresses completed action in the past, or acts as a past attributive participle ("having done"). 4-way harmony.

examples.english: I went to the library yesterday.
He has just arrived.
I haven't seen this movie.

exceptions: Confusing -сан (reported/neutral past) with -лаа (witnessed immediate past).
Negating with биш vs үгүй: as predicate it takes үгүй (e.g. Би яваагүй).

keyPoints: Consonant stems: + бал / бэл / бол / бөл (e.g. сурвал, үзвэл)
Vowel stems and stems ending in r/l/v: + вал / вэл / вол / вөл (e.g. очвол, суувал)

rules.title: Conditional Converb (-бал, -бэл, -бол, -бөл / -вал, -вэл, -вол, -вөл)
rules.summary: Expresses "if / when" conditions. Distinguishes consonant vs vowel stems with -бал/-вал.
rules.explanation: Expresses "if / when" conditions. Distinguishes consonant vs vowel stems with -бал/-вал.

examples.english: If time permits, I will come.
If you study diligently, you will pass your exam.

exceptions: Confusing hypothetical conditional (-вал) with concessive (-вч "although").
Violating 4-way harmony in the suffix vowel.

grammarOverview.summary: Mongolian constructs lengthy periodic sentences by stringing non-finite converbal clauses that terminate on a single finite main verb.
keyPoints: Subordinate clause 1 (Converb) + Subordinate clause 2 (Converb) + Main finite clause (Verb + finite ending)
Temporal sequence: -аад -> Logical condition: -вал -> Purpose: -хаар -> Main verb.

rules.title: Complex Converb Chaining & Discourse Hierarchy

rules.summary: Mongolian constructs lengthy periodic sentences by stringing non-finite converbal clauses that terminate on a single finite main verb.
rules.explanation: Mongolian constructs lengthy periodic sentences by stringing non-finite converbal clauses that terminate on a single finite main verb.

examples.cyrillic: Өглөө босоод, цайгаа чанаж уугаад, ажилдаа гарлаа.
examples.english: Having gotten up in the morning, brewed and drank tea, he departed for work.
examples.breakdown: Өглөө босоод, цайгаа чанаж уугаад, ажилдаа гарлаа.

examples.english: When the sun rose, the birds began to chirp.

grammarOverview.summary: Mongolian vowels are divided into masculine (а, о, у), feminine (э, ө, ү), and neutral (и, й). Suffixes must agree with root vowels.
keyPoints: Masculine root (contains а, о, у) -> Takes masculine suffixes (-аар, -аас, -тай, -даг, etc.)
Feminine root (contains э, ө, ү) -> Takes feminine suffixes (-ээр, -өөс, -тэй, -дэг, etc.)
Neutral vowel (и) harmonizes with feminine suffixes if alone, or defers to existing masculine/feminine vowels.

grammarOverview.summary: Expresses possession, origin, or association ("of / 's"). Formed with -ын/-ийн/-ний/-ны depending on terminal phonemes.
keyPoints: Consonant stems (masculine): + ын (e.g. адуу -> адууны, ном -> номын)
Consonant stems (feminine): + ийн (e.g. гэр -> гэрийн, эгч -> эгчийн)
Stems ending in long vowels or diphthongs: + н / -ны / -ний
Stems ending in short vowels: usually drop final short vowel + ын/ийн
